Hello HN!

I’m sure many of you have used AI agent apps like OpenClaw, Claude Code, or Codex on your PCs, but you rarely see AI agents running on the iOS platform. That’s why I created an agent app that runs exclusively on iOS—it doesn’t require a separate computer or server; it runs entirely on your iPhone.

Plus, in the latest version, we’ve become the first to integrate Jev AI—a very popular decision-making AI—on the App Store.

We invite you to try it out, and we look forward to your feedback.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/chatlo-ai-chat-agent/id6771188...

story_text.value:
hi everyone, been building this project for the last ~1.5 months (cc+superpowers all the way)

it is an open effort to find a program that can reliably win NetHack 3.6.6: you can write a bot by hand, let claude code / codex / opencode improve one, or build your own harness that improves the thing that improves the bot

me and my lab switched to the goal-based research this year (we worked a lot in the idea-based framework for a last couple of years) -- and decided that we would like to tackle the NetHack, it is one of those nasty roguelike that is still somehow not solved with all fancy AI models (yes, even astra) -- probably on the way something useful will appear

you can pull someone else's bot, run experiments locally and register the results. every registered program is linked to your github repo and exact source commit

i always wanted to try building something that will use github as both social and storage layer (and it seems to work quite well in our case, simplified things a bit and i think this approach is quite cool)

there is a shared frontier across 73 starting identities -- your bots dont have to be the best at everything to contribute something useful, e.g. if you love to roleplay gnomes only, so be it

to make thing easier (for both harness devs and people who are just playing around), we provide a loop that does some sort of an evolutionary optimization process (quality-diversity, etc), ofc you don't have to use it. but you can start with in minutes (given you have codex or claude subs)

you can also bring your own search, your own harness, whatever -- the common ground is the evaluation. public seeds are there for people to overfit (in nethack even overfitting is hard), and we separately re-evaluate on hidden seeds to check whether the improvements actually transfer

one of my goals was to actually try to make it at least a bit fun -- hope you enjoy the web-site and easter eggs

story_text.value:
I've really enjoyed and am quite proud on where this project has become. I started this 6 years ago and it's gone through many iterations to get to this point. This latest iteration of what you see if you click and view the page has been roughly 6 months of development and testing and tweaking. I recently had an overhaul to the graphics and UX so I considered that as something valid to share again with you all.

The tech stack is react, with tailwindcss and hosted on cloudflare. I learned a whole lot about page speed and optimization, because it was just about a month ago I got feedback that the website was slow- my FCP was 34 seconds on mobile! This time around it isn't my first rodeo, and I was able to learn some tricks like font subsetting, dynamic javascript imports, setting explicit heights/widths of images to prevent content shifts, among other things in order to get my page speed in the mid 90's. This may be old knowledge if you've done this before, but it's been a good journey and I'm using this project not only for my own purposes, but also to grow and learn more about pieces of web development I never considered before.

It's not AI, and it's been a labor of love.

title.value: Show HN: Recipe Card Creator

story_text.value:
Hey HN!

Owner of a first generation Logitech MX Master [1] and MX Keys S here, frequently switching between two Macs. Every time the mouse has to be turned over to access the button at the bottom, and keyboard has to be switched on it's own.

Logitech finally released an Options+ feature [2, 3] to switch multiple peripherals at the same time, with a single key press. The only problem - my ol' reliable isn't supported. It's a Unifying device, and only Bolt is officially supported. [4]

So, I made a fix - The Mouse Is Coming Too. There are 3 mini-apps, each coresponding to a different host device. Running any of them will switch both the mouse and the keyboard to a given host. They are mappable to "Open application" in Options+, so a programmable key can be used to trigger them.

Tested with MX Master and MX Keys S, but should work with any models recognised by Options+

[1] v1, bough some 9 years ago, and released in 2025. Still going strong after some ~9 years, micro-USB to USB-C conversion, skates replacement, stuck thumb button [5], and more than a few falls

[2] Yes, I should switch to something better

[3] https://marketplace.logi.com/releasenotes/optionsplus/en#2.6...

[4] To make it a bit more absurd, "easy switch" for this mouse already exists and works, but is accessible only through Options+ Action ring. Tried giving it a fair chance, but it's too cumbersome.

[5] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WNP1mnZx58

title.value: Show HN: The Mouse Is Coming Too – Easy Switch for Legacy Logitech Devices
